findings.title: Hidden attributes are filtered out only while a search query is set.
findings.body: `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` is applied only inside the `filter` that runs after the early `if (!searchQuery.trim()) return sorted;`. With an empty search box, which is the default view, `is_segment`, `project_id` and `received` still appear. They disappear only once the user types a query. Apply the hidden-attribute filter before the early return, for example `const sorted = sortAttributes(attributes).filter(a => !HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(a.name));`.

findings.title: Zipping error_ids with get_multi values can pair IDs with the wrong events.
findings.body: `nodestore.backend.get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node id. Backends may leave out keys that were not found, and dict order is not guaranteed to match the request order. `zip(error_ids, events.values())` then pairs an error id with another event's data, or shifts every id after a missing one, so wrong titles and timestamps are attached to error ids. Look up each event by its node id instead: `for eid, nid in zip(error_ids, node_ids): data = events.get(nid)`.

findings.title: Error timestamps in seconds are compared with replay event timestamps in milliseconds.
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` takes `timestamp` from the nodestore event data, which is in epoch seconds. Replay recording events (rrweb frames) carry `timestamp` in epoch milliseconds. Because of this, `error_events[idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)` is true for almost every error, so all errors are output before the first breadcrumb. The chronological merge, which is the point of this change, never happens, and the LLM gets errors out of order. Convert one side so both use the same unit, for example multiply the error timestamp by 1000 before the comparison.

findings.title: Second placeholder group loses its gap and vertical alignment.
findings.body: The removed `FlexBox` set `align-items: center` and `gap: space(1)` on both placeholder groups. The new second `<Flex>` (line 27) has neither prop, so the three 100px placeholders now sit flush against each other. The loaded container on line 93 also no longer gets `align` or `gap`. To keep the old layout, add `align="center" gap={space(1)}` to these `Flex` elements.
